name: Polar sea ice
summary: Both poles well below normal sea-ice extent, but not at record lows
state: On 31 Oct Arctic sea-ice extent was 7.84 million km², 1.73 million below the 1981–2010 average and the sixth-lowest for the date. Antarctic extent was 1.62 million below average, second-lowest for the date. Neither pole is at a record low.
for_you: Low sea ice amplifies warming and can disturb weather patterns, including European winters.
why: Sea ice reflects sunlight and regulates ocean circulation; record lows accelerate warming.
drivers: Air and ocean temperatures, winds, season.

rubric.alert: Either pole at a record low for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Arctic and Antarctic extent anomalies both above −1.0 million km² vs 1981–2010.
